content.comment_body: Hello, everyone. My second question is: How can I create HTML and CSS files on my computer and upload these to the [product_name] SD card without using [product_name] Web Editor? I'm currently taking HTML/CSS courses and would like to design visually appealing pages for my [product_name] web server. Thanks in advance.

For your setup, make sure you have the current [product_name] version with the extended web server features. You can utilize a free application provided by [company_name], the [product_name] Web Editor. There are instructions included in the download that offer a general overview on creating HTML5 pages yourself.

Hello all. Thanks for your response—it was very helpful. To assist others, I want to point out that the CSS and HTML files are stored on the computer that runs [product_name] Web Server Editor. Check in the folder NetBeansProjects/[project_name] to find all files. Initially, I thought the files were compiled and loaded into [product_name] similar to how automation files are managed, leading me to try to access the [product_name] SD card for editing, which isn't the correct approach. Now I see I can directly edit my CSS and HTML files to improve my pages.

analysis.insight_summary: Individuals working with [product_name] web servers aimed to enhance web page design but were unclear about where the HTML/CSS files reside and how they're processed. A common misunderstanding was the belief that files needed to be edited directly on the [product_name] SD card rather than using the recommended workflow with the [product_name] Web Editor. This lack of clarity around file management made customizing the web pages more challenging until proper information was provided.
analysis.user_expectations: Users wish for a simple and direct method to access and modify HTML/CSS files for their [product_name] web server, ideally wanting the flexibility to do so without always having to rely on the [product_name] Web Editor.
